notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Build the play around a credible question and an owned reply.
intro: A proposed enterprise-play workbench for Edra: turn sourced process hypotheses into coordinated AE and BDR experiments, then evaluate qualified outcomes.
queueIntro: These fictional organizations illustrate research about business processes. No internal tickets, messages, customer systems or process data are accessed.
workbenchIntro: Review the account hypothesis, buying group and follow-up plan before proposing a play. This local demo sends no messages and operates no customer agents.
firstBuild: An evidence-backed play the AE helps shape
firstBody: Connect an enterprise process question with a dated why-now signal, an agreed buying group and an explicit follow-up owner before launch.

fields.label: Why-now signal has a dated business source
Buying group and missing roles mapped
Message ties evidence to a credible question
AE and BDR agree on the play and follow-up
Scale and stop criteria agreed before the test

rules.title: Name the operating process
rules.next: Frame a support, IT service or operational knowledge problem rather than a broad AI-transformation claim.

rules.title: Ground the why-now hypothesis
rules.next: Separate a public organizational change from confirmed demand for process automation.

rules.title: Map the buying group
rules.next: Record the operating sponsor, technical reviewer and missing roles without inventing contacts.

rules.title: Rewrite the account-specific message
rules.next: Make the link from evidence to discovery explicit. Do not claim to know the prospect’s internal process failures.

rules.title: Agree on follow-up before launch
rules.next: Confirm the account list, receiving owner and reply handling before generating campaign activity.

rules.title: Define the experiment decision
rules.next: Choose a qualified-outcome metric and limits for negative replies, incorrect research and team workload.

ready.title: Ready for a coordinated play review
ready.next: The AE and BDR can review the hypothesis, audience and follow-up plan. Launch and scaling decisions remain with the responsible team.

experiments.name: Process-specific enterprise messaging
experiments.hypothesis: A credible operating question improves discovery quality.
experiments.treatment: Sourced process hypothesis and buying-group question
experiments.primary: Qualified opportunities per original account cohort
experiments.guardrail: Incorrect personalization and unsupported internal-process claims
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Sales-aligned play design
experiments.hypothesis: Agreeing on follow-up before launch turns relevant replies into owned next steps.
experiments.treatment: AE/BDR plan agreed before the test
experiments.primary: Qualified replies with an accepted next action
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Choose a process and buying group
roadmap.body: Work with sales on a narrow enterprise hypothesis, source contract and qualification definition.

roadmap.title: Run one coordinated play
roadmap.body: Build research and message proposals with evidence attached. Agree on follow-up and stop conditions before launch.
roadmap.measure: Relevant replies and owned next steps

roadmap.title: Scale or retire with evidence
roadmap.body: Review qualified opportunities, negative signals and operating effort by cohort. Keep the playbook and research current.
roadmap.measure: Qualified pipeline and cost of maintaining the play

records.name: Alder Services
records.context: A fictional company is consolidating support operations after an acquisition.
records.question: How does process knowledge move across the combined team?

records.name: Cedar Commerce
records.context: The brief says AI transformation without naming an operating process.
records.question: Which repeated process would be worth understanding first?

records.name: Willow Software
records.context: The why-now line is based on an undated assumption.
records.question: What current business source supports this timing?

records.name: Elm Industries
records.context: Only an executive sponsor is mapped; technical review ownership is missing.
records.question: Who understands the operating systems and process constraints?

records.name: Birch Systems
records.context: A message claims to know internal failure rates.
records.question: What evidence-based question could replace that unsupported claim?

records.name: Juniper Group
records.context: The campaign is ready but no BDR has accepted reply ownership.
records.question: Who will act on relevant replies and with what next step?

metricsTitle: A play earns expansion through qualified outcomes.
metricsIntro: Illustrative decision ledger; each cohort uses the same observation window.
metricsNotes: All counts and decisions are synthetic, not Edra performance.
A small sample is directional. Review account selection, timing and reply quality before claiming causality.
Scale decisions should include negative replies, source accuracy and AE/BDR capacity, not only response rate.
aiApplication: At Edra, I would use a small research swarm to prepare sourced enterprise-process hypotheses for AE and BDR review. The feedback loop would compare qualified outcomes, preserve rejection reasons and promote changes only after an evidence check.
